thread:
oncall-bot: 🔔 Alert: routing-fallback-errors detected for capacity-tier selection (severity: P2). 170+ errors/min for tenant: tenant-45A starting 2026-03-15T09:33:09Z. Auto-escalating to oncall.
Maya: I'm on it, grabbing context. Which pool is tenant-45A supposed to be in? :thinking:
Devon: tenant-45A should be pinned to dedicated-pool-east-2 (reserved). Logs show requests are being routed to hosted-pool-eu-west-1 instead.
Maya: ugh. That explains increased latency + 5xxs. Can we get a quick impact estimate? Who's watching dashboards?
Victor: I see spikes on routing-errors and KV cache misses for that tenant. Error = routing_policy_mismatch. ~1200 failed tokens in the last 5m. Likely customers seeing 502/504s.
Tilly: paging alex for routing-policy override. @Alex can you join? Taking page for mitigation if needed.
Alex: on call. I'm looking at the policy graph. There's a canary rule that overrides tier affinity when hosted capacity < 10% free; it incorrectly matches the tenant tag `affinity:dedicated` due to a regex mismatch.
Maya: can we apply a temporary fix to route tenant-45A back to dedicated pool? I'll coordinate comms.
Alex: I'll apply a temporary sticky-binding. Running:
```
# pin tenant to the dedicated pool for 15m
redwoodctl routing set-tenant-pool --tenant tenant-45A --pool dedicated-pool-east-2 --ttl 900
```
Alex: applied. Confirming route table shows tenant-45A -> dedicated-pool-east-2 (sticky:true, ttl:900).
Devon: pulling proxy logs. Snippet:
```
[09:33:12Z] router: request tenant=tenant-45A model=redwood-alpha variant=quant2 intended_pool=dedicated-pool-east-2 matched_rule=canary-affinity-override -> routed_to=hosted-pool-eu-west-1
[09:34:01Z] error: routing_policy_mismatch: expected pool dedicated-pool-east-2 but assigned hosted-pool-eu-west-1
```
Victor: after the pin, we see dropped errors for tenant-45A down to baseline. Latency back to normal for this tenant.
Maya: good. Can SRE confirm no other tenants are affected by the same policy? Run a quick grep across recent matches.
Tilly: running query: `SELECT count(*) FROM routing_matches WHERE rule='canary-affinity-override' AND match_time > now()-10m` -> 37 tenants matched, 2 with dedicated affinity tag (tenant-45A and tenant-9C).
Devon: it's a race condition in the rule evaluation order. When capacity probes return stale free-capacity, the canary rule's condition flips and applies an `override=true` label. That override logic doesn't re-check tenant-affinity tag, so it overrides pinned tenants.
Alex: created immediate guard: `if tenant.has_affinity: skip_override`. Pushing hotfix to route-eval service, will 2-step deploy (canary + roll).
sre-bot: deploy-started: route-eval  -> commit 9f3b2a, canary region=us-west-2, expected 3-5m
Victor: monitoring metrics for route-eval canary now.
Maya: customer impact update: two customers (tenant-45A, tenant-9C) experienced increased 5xxs and timeouts for about 12 minutes. We opened an incident with CS and alerted reps. No data exfiltration, only availability impact.
Tilly: handing primary to Devon for postmortem. I'll stay on until after rollback verification. @Devon please take lead on RCA and customer comms.
Devon: taking handoff. I'll collect logs, timeline, and produce a short RCA. Preliminary root cause: canary-affinity-override rule evaluated when capacity probe returned stale low-capacity, causing override to misapply to tenants with explicit affinity tags. Fix = respect tenant affinity in override and tighten probe expiry.
Alex: can confirm hotfix applied to canary and rollout passed canary checks. Rolling to global now.
sre-bot: deploy-success: route-eval canary passed checks; rollout to 70% started.
Maya: action items captured:
- Devon: full RCA + timeline (Due EOD).
- Alex: write unit tests for rule ordering + regression test for affinity pinned tenants (Due 48h).
- Infrastructure: lower capacity-probe TTL to 20s (Due 24h).
- CS: confirm customer notifications and credit if requested (Assigned: Maya).
Victor: adding log query snippets to incident notes for follow-up.
Maya: nice quick mitigation. Leaving incident open for RCA tracking. If any more anomalies pop, ping #incidents.
Devon: closing the active pager, will update thread when RCA ready. Thanks everyone. :wave:
